# AzureFunction

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_component_agents.py from xrds/azurefunction.meta.yaml; edit the sidecar, not this file. -->

Onboards an Azure Functions app: a source repo with a container scaffold for the chosen runtime, a SecretStore request, the TektonCICD child, and with spec.target.enabled the AzureContainerAppTarget it deploys to.

## How it is requested

A Backstage template or an XR request in the dev cluster's tenants repo; it onboards the app onto the dev cluster.

## Outputs

- `sourceRepo`: `{name}`. The GitHub repository holding the app's source and its scaffold, under the platform's GitHub owner.
- `tektonCicd`: `{name}-tektoncicd`. The composed TektonCICD child XR in the same namespace; DevClusterReady and CicdOnboarded are copied from it.
- `target`: `{name}-target`. The composed AzureContainerAppTarget child XR when spec.target.enabled; its status carries the cloud names (function, URL).

## Where named objects come from

- Repository `{name}-src`: composed by this composition.
- TektonCICD `{name}-tektoncicd`: composed by this composition.
- AzureContainerAppTarget `{name}-target`: composed by this composition (when `spec.target.enabled` is `True`).

## Conditions

Besides Crossplane's Ready and Synced. Reasons are a closed set:

- `DevClusterReady`: `DevClusterReady` (True), `DevClusterNotReady` (False).
- `CicdOnboarded`: `CicdOnboarded` (True), `CicdOnboardingPending` (False).
- `TargetReady`: `TargetPending` (False), `AzureContainerAppTargetReady` (True), `AzureContainerAppTargetProvisioning` (False).

## Verify a live XR

```
tools/airframe-verify azurefunction <namespace>/<name> [--context CTX]
```

Read-only. Steps, after the implicit `xr-synced` check:

- `dev-cluster-ready` (condition): The XR's DevClusterReady condition is True (DevClusterReady).
- `cicd-onboarded` (condition): The XR's CicdOnboarded condition is True (CicdOnboarded): the tenants repo carries the app's identity.yaml.
- `source-repo` (resource): The Repository managed resource {name}-src is Ready, so the GitHub source repository exists.
- `target-ready` (condition): With spec.target.enabled, the XR's TargetReady condition has reason AzureContainerAppTargetReady. Only when `spec.target.enabled` is `True`.

## Editing this composition

- Edit `compositions/azurefunction/templates/`, never the inline blocks in `composition.yaml`: `python3 tools/build-compositions azurefunction` splices them.
- `python3 tools/test_compositions.py --update azurefunction` regenerates `example/expected/`; review that diff like code, it is the behaviour change.
- `python3 tools/test_sidecars.py` fails if a template change breaks a name this sidecar promises.
- Shared with other compositions (symlinks into `compositions/_shared/`): `00-devcluster-gate.yaml`, `00-scaffold-done.yaml`, `secretstore-xr.yaml`, `status.yaml`, `tekton-cicd-child.yaml`, `zz-scaffold-ledger.yaml`.
- Scaffold files (RepositoryFiles whose managementPolicies lack Update) are composed once, recorded in status.scaffold.done and then retired; keep a new scaffold file create-once and wrap it in the ledger gate (compositions/_shared/README.md).
- Never give a RepositoryFile a Delete policy: a prune once deleted cicd.yaml from five app repos. Keep the crossplane.io/external-name pin so a cluster rebuild adopts existing files instead of overwriting them.
- Four templates are symlinks into compositions/_shared/ (dev-cluster gate, SecretStore request, TektonCICD child, status); per-kind differences go in 00-inputs.yaml, never in the shared file.
- With spec.target.enabled the composition also composes an AzureContainerAppTarget named <name>-target; its TargetReady is copied to this XR.
